abstract: For rational numbers write d(1,xy) = |1-xy|. A set of rationals in which d(1,xy) is a nonzero square for every pair is a mixed set: the same thing as a Diophantine set over Q(i) with all entries in iQ. Two constructions of mixed octuples with one zero are known here, from a right triangle with a 120-degree triangle (Paper 89) and with the golden ratio (Paper 21); Paper 89 places both on the curve Y^2 = X(X+U^4)(X+V^4) with a point S of order four. The towers of both branches live on one family of quartics W^2 = t^4 + (3-h)t^2 + h, h in {3,-1}, and the passage from tower to tower is the single map t -> (L+W)/U, proved to be translation by a fixed point on the Jacobian; every tower we know is a multiple of that point. The six links of the second kind in every floor are read off the descent class (-1,-1,1) of S. The conditions on a base force E_{U,V} with a Pythagorean pair and an explicit curve of genus five for the base point. The 2-Selmer groups of the five curves of the first three towers are certified by a terminating local decision with a proved depth bound, giving rank one; within the subgroup generated by the base point nothing exists beyond the floors. The four-and-four shape is proved for every floor, and conjectured for the reflections of the floors, where it reduces to a statement about one boundary member. No rational septuple is constructed or excluded.

title: The Pythagorean puzzle: d(1,xy) in Q*^2. One curve, one recursion, and the two infinities of the mixed octuples (fifth version)
